description:
Classify how an organization builds or uses AI against the risk tiers of the EU AI
Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). Returns the highest tier triggered, every tier with
whether it applies, the compliance deadline and maximum penalty for each, whether the
organization leans provider or deployer, and which specific answers drove the result.

Every parameter's description is the question as a person is asked it, and its enum is
the permitted values. Ask the person the questions rather than guessing: a wrong answer to
the Annex III domains or the prohibited practices list changes the tier.

Results are informational and not legal advice. Relay the disclaimer field with any
answer built from this.

aiFrequency.description: How often does your business use AI? Including internal tools. Count anything where AI helps with analysis, drafting, scheduling, coding, research, or any task, even if customers never see it.

annexDomains.description: Does AI help make or influence any decisions about people in your business? Select any that apply. This is about decisions that meaningfully affect a person, where AI plays a role in the outcome.

biometricUse.description: Does your business use AI that recognizes or analyzes people's physical characteristics? For example, systems that identify people by face or voice, or that analyze physical or biometric characteristics.

industryOther.description: Free text naming the industry. Only meaningful when `industry` is "other".

prohibited.description: Could any of your AI uses fall into these categories? These are uses the EU has banned outright. Most businesses will select none. Select any you are unsure about. Selecting one is not a verdict. It flags something worth an urgent closer look.

roleSignal.description: Which best describes how your business gets the AI it uses? This is about where your AI comes from, not how it works. 'Building or heavily customizing' means your team trains, fine-tunes, or substantially modifies AI models. 'Using tools others built' means you use AI products or features made by other companies, roughly as they come.

transparencyContent.description: Does your business use AI to create or edit content that you publish or send out? For example, marketing copy, social posts, product descriptions, images, audio, or video where AI created or significantly changed what you publish or send.

transparencyInteraction.description: Does your business use AI that talks to your customers or the public? For example, a chatbot on your website, an AI assistant in your app, or an automated system that answers customer questions by phone or message.

title: Classify EU AI Act risk
